title: Calldata whose bytes tail has nonzero padding, which solc 0.8.24's decoder accepts, makes holon.replay_fragments.model_call evaluate the model with no arguments: real revertBatch succeeds while the model predicts the revert 'count must be nonzero'
reproduction: cd <repo at C> && export BEND_NO_TELEMETRY=1 GOPROXY=off PATH=$HOME/.holon/bin:$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH; python -m holon audit hostile-input --milestone M3 --round 3 --spec audit/rounds/M3/round3/a2_spec.json --target 5e2436f9808d4c08a45de8c26ae1dcf9b2fde1dc (committed audit/rounds/M3/round3/a2.json; generator audit/rounds/M3/round3/a2_mkspec.py): c40, revertBatch(header of batch 1, 1) by the owner with the 249-byte header's tail padded by seven 0xff bytes, is real ok (6 slots written) and model revert ['error', 'count must be nonzero'] (verdict disagree, differ ['status']); c41, the same call padded with zeros, agrees (ok, ok). c35, finalizeBatch(genesis header) with 0xff padding: real Panic(0x11) (the `_batchIndex - 1` underflow at Rollup.sol:636), model 'Empty batch header'; c39, the same call cleanly encoded, agrees on Panic(0x11). c32 and c33 (a length or an offset past the calldata): real revert with empty data (the ABI decoder), model 'Empty batch header'. Cause: holon.evm_abi.decode_args rejects a bytes tail with dirty padding in strict and non-strict mode (its docstring says solc's calldata decoder reverts on it; for a bytes calldata tail it does not), and model_call's fallback for calldata that does not decode is args = {} (meant for calldata shorter than its arguments), so the model runs the action on defaulted arguments. Direct: holon.evm_abi.decode_args([{'name': '_batchHeader', 'type': 'bytes'}, {'name': '_count', 'type': 'uint256'}], <c40's calldata after the selector>) raises AbiError('dirty bytes padding') with strict=True and strict=False, while c41's zero-padded calldata decodes to _count 1 and the 249-byte header.
plan_or_paper_ref: whitepaper §9.5 A2 (whether the model's partiality matches the code's), §8.7 refinement evidence through native replay
suggested_fix: Decode a bytes or string tail without checking its padding, as solc's calldata decoder does (keep the dirty-padding check for elementary values only), and let model_call return no model call (the case 'unsupported', with the reason) for calldata that does not decode, instead of evaluating the action on empty arguments; add c40's calldata to the step refinement's boundary corpus.

It copies the committed proof of L_sym_tau_L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle_getMessageEnqueueTimestamp (whose record lists bendtt result "failed") to scratch and prints: unsafe_env_files catches a plain .env but returns [] for .env.local; holon.bend.check_verdict is False (the pinned BendTT kernel rejects the counter-law) with no .env.local, and True (ALL PROOFS CHECK) once a .env.local sets BENDTT=<a fake kernel that prints ALL PROOFS CHECK>. check_verdict is the second kernel used by gate G7, G11V and holon.records.kernels. holon/consumers.py already strips .env.* (NO_BUN_CONFIG) as unsafe Bun config, but holon.bend.unsafe_env_files (GENV) matches only bunfig.toml and .env (holon/bend.py UNSAFE_ENV_FILES).
plan_or_paper_ref: whitepaper Appendix G (GENV); M0_SPEC.md §7 (GENV); AGENTS.md rule 8
suggested_fix: Make holon.bend.unsafe_env_files reject every .env* file (as holon/consumers.py NO_BUN_CONFIG already does: shutil.ignore_patterns('.env','.env.*','bunfig.toml')), so GENV refuses any dotenv variant anywhere under root; and have holon.bend._env / the checker launcher clear BENDTT and BEND_LIB so a .env* loaded from cwd cannot reach the kernel path even if one slips past the scan.
lead_adjudication: fixed by I97 (#122, landed via #123): GENV refuses bunfig.toml and every .env* name at any depth; the checker runs with an allowlisted environment, the pinned BendTT and an empty working directory; round 4's repro no longer flips the verdict.

reproduction: At C with the pinned toolchain: python -m holon audit mutation --milestone M3 --round 4 --spec audit/rounds/M3/round4/a1_parts/g3_block_context_fields_swapped.spec.json --target 4dada37b5a1cb84a3b4faccc333e7e8467d116d5 --out /tmp/g3.json . The one cross-component path that reads the block-context height, a go_recompute law for BatchData.DataHashV2, is not generated: gen/M3/gox/basis.json lists candidate L_par_gorc_data_hash_BatchData_DataHashV2 with reason alloc_preimage.

round: M3/round5 (Claude agent, session claude-subagent/M3-round5/2026-11-09, same family)
aspect: calldata decoding at the Rollup entry points
title: The Rollup model's call interface runs an action with no arguments whenever HOLON's ABI decoder refuses its calldata, and that decoder refuses calldata solc accepts: with one non-zero byte in the zero padding of a bytes tail, commitBatch and revertBatch succeed on the real Rollup and revert on the model; for an offset or a bytes length past the end of the calldata, which solc refuses in its decoder with empty revert data, the model reverts at a later require instead.
reproduction: At C (bc89b12d), with the pinned toolchain: python -m holon audit hostile-input --milestone M3 --round 5 --spec audit/rounds/M3/round5/a2_spec.json prints '53 hostile input(s) ...; 49 agree, 4 disagree, 0 unsupported'. In audit/rounds/M3/round5/a2.json: a35_commit_dirty_tail_padding (the committed witness corpus's commitBatch calldata, results/M3/L_disch_ext_rollup_132_d953872f_onlyOwner.json witness step 0, with its last byte, which is padding of the 249-byte parentBatchHeader tail, set to 0x01): model revert [error, 'Empty batch header'], real ok with 8 storage writes; a36_revert_dirty_tail_padding (revertBatch(batch 1's header, 1) by the owner after one commitBatch, last padding byte 0x01): model revert [error, 'count must be nonzero'], real ok with 6 writes; a40_revert_canonical_calldata (the same call with clean padding): agree, both ok, 6 writes. a29_revert_offset_out_of_bounds (bytes offset 2^256-1) and a37_revert_bytes_length_past_end (bytes length 300, 256 bytes present): model revert [error, 'count must be nonzero'], real revert [raw, 0x]. The cause in the code: holon/evm_abi.py decode raises AbiError('dirty bytes padding') for a bytes tail in strict and in non-strict mode (its docstring says solc's calldata decoder reverts on it; a35 and a36 show it does not), and holon/replay_fragments.py model_call then hands the model args {} ('calldata shorter than its arguments gives none'), so the compiled model runs the action with every argument absent. No law quantifies over raw calldata and every committed witness, replay and refinement step uses canonical encodings, so no recorded status moves (results/M2/refinement/extracted.json lists no disagreement on its corpus, which has no such calldata). Cross-reference, read only after this line was written: the same defect as F-M3-11 (round 3, revertBatch with seven 0xff padding bytes), open at C; this round reproduces it independently at C and adds commitBatch (a35) and the past-the-end cases (a29, a37). Status duplicate for that reason.
plan_or_paper_ref: whitepaper §9.5 A2 (the model's partiality against the code's), §8.7 (refinement through native replay), §5.1 (domain coherence at an interface carrier)
suggested_fix: Decode a bytes or string tail as solc's calldata decoder does (offset and length bounds checked, tail padding not checked); when the decoder refuses calldata, give the model side the decoder's outcome (a revert with empty data) instead of running the action with no arguments; add dirty tail padding and offsets or lengths past the end to the refinement corpus, so that a model-side decoding error shows as a refinement disagreement.

round: M3/round5 (Claude agent, session claude-subagent/M3-round5/2026-11-09, same family)
aspect: PAR round-trip basis under a misplaced decoder
title: A Go decoder that reads the wrong offset removes the round-trip obligation it breaks instead of refuting it: mutant m01 (BatchHeaderBytes.L1MessagePopped reads b[10:18]) drops all six L1MessagePopped round-trip laws and that decoder from the six cross-component codec laws, and m12 (HeightFromBlockContextBytes reads [1:9]) drops both BuildBlockContext round trips; holon audit mutation counts each as detected (a derivation change), but on the mutant code no law states the broken round trip, and the one law that moves on m01 is refuted only because the derivation dropped its L1MessagePopped premise, at a witness whose two inputs differ in that field while both encoders are unchanged.
reproduction: At C: python -m holon audit mutation --milestone M3 --round 5 --spec audit/rounds/M3/round5/a1_spec.json writes a1.json with m01_go_getter_offset 'derivation change: 6 law(s) dropped' (L_par_rt_{BatchCache_createBatchHeaderWithSequencerSetHash,BatchHeaderV0_Bytes,BatchHeaderV1_Bytes,enc_sol}_BatchHeaderBytes_L1MessagePopped_v*) and '6 law(s) statement changed' (the six L_par_cc_*), no law added; m12_go_height_offset '2 law(s) dropped' (L_par_gort_BuildBlockContext_HeightFromBlockContextBytes_0 and _1), none added. The only document change m01 makes is /go/codecs/decoders/5/reads/0/offset (and the getter's path terms). With the mutant's trees kept (same command with --spec audit/rounds/M3/round5/a1_spec_m01_kept.json --keep-trees --out .../a1_m01_kept.json): the mutant tree's laws/M3 holds 270 laws, without the six L1MessagePopped round trips (round5/a1/m01/mutant_law_ids.txt); its L_par_cc_BatchHeaderV1_Bytes_enc_sol_v1_pinned lists the decoders without CODEC.BatchHeaderBytes_L1MessagePopped and has lost the premise h.BatchHeaderV0.L1MessagePopped == k.l1MessagePopped (11 premises, C has 12); `python -m holon run --milestone M3 --laws L_par_cc_BatchHeaderV1_Bytes_enc_sol_v1_pinned` in that tree prints REFUTED (bend2 and BendTT checked) at h.BatchHeaderV0.L1MessagePopped 0x090a0b0c0d0e0f10 against k.l1MessagePopped 0x0b0c0d0e0f101112 (round5/a1/m01/mutant_record_*.json); at C the law is PROVED. holon audit mutation re-runs only laws whose statement did not change, so it ran none of these. Cross-reference, read only after this line was written: the same defect as F-M3-10 (round 3, whose m05 is this round's m12), open at C; this round reproduces it independently at C and adds that the one law m01 moves is refuted only through the premise the derivation dropped. Status duplicate for that reason.
plan_or_paper_ref: whitepaper §9.5 A1 (confirm that the corresponding obstruction appears), §5.1 PAR round trip, Thm 6.4 (fundamental cycles are complete)
suggested_fix: Derive the round trip of every encoder and decoder over the same carrier and field (the decoded view's getter) whatever their offsets, so that an offset mismatch is a law that is REFUTED; take a cross-component codec law's field premises from the encoders' fields, not from the decoders that happen to align with them; and in holon audit mutation re-run the laws whose statement changed or that were dropped (or report 'obligation removed') instead of counting every derivation change as detected.

round: M3/round5 (Claude agent, session claude-subagent/M3-round5/2026-11-09, same family)
aspect: FACT kernel basis under a dropped guard
title: Removing commitState's blob guard removes the FACT kernel law that the mutant violates instead of refuting it: with require(blobhash(0) == bytes32(0)) made vacuous (m07), the extracted commitState loses its blobhash edge, and holon derive no longer states L_fact_kernel_Rollup_commitState_committedBatches_blobhash (PROVED at C: equal committedBatches values deliver equal blobhash lists), which the mutant breaks, since commitState then commits the stored blob hash whatever blobs the call carries; holon audit mutation counts the drop as detected, but on such code no FACT law covers commitState's commitment.
reproduction: At C: python -m holon audit mutation --milestone M3 --round 5 --spec audit/rounds/M3/round5/a1_spec.json writes a1.json with m07_sol_dropped_blob_guard (contracts/contracts/l1/rollup/Rollup.sol:276 'require(blobhash(0) == bytes32(0), ' -> 'require(true, '): verdict detected, obstruction 'derivation change: 1 law(s) dropped', dropped [L_fact_kernel_Rollup_commitState_committedBatches_blobhash], added [], statement_changed []; the re-extracted spec/M2/facts/morph_rollup.extracted.json changes at /actions/10/edges[len 3 -> 2] (commitState's blobhash edge) and /actions/10/guards/3. At C the law is PROVED because the guard makes every successful commitState carry no blob. The counterexample the mutant admits is argued from the code, not run on a mutant tree (the shared disk did not allow keeping one): from the state of this round's A4 representative (audit/rounds/M3/round5/a4/rep_fact_commitState.json: prefix commitBatch, revertBatch, where two commitState calls succeed and commit equal committedBatches values), one call without a blob and one carrying a blob both succeed once the guard is gone, commit the same value (commitState hashes the stored blob hash, not the call's blobs) and deliver different blobhash lists. Related to F-M3-10 and F-M3-17 (the PAR codec round trips), here in rule FACT: the consumer is taken from the action's own blobhash read, so removing the read removes the obligation.
plan_or_paper_ref: whitepaper §9.5 A1, §5.5 FACT (every consumer in the commitment's scope), §11.3 ('no blob' and 'zero blob' conflated)
suggested_fix: Take FACT's consumers in a commitment's scope from what the action's transaction delivers (its blobs reach L2 derivation whether or not the action reads blobhash), not only from the action's own reads, so a removed check leaves the obligation in place to be refuted; and have holon audit mutation report a dropped law as 'obligation removed' rather than as detected.
